title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy produced by arc melting and homogenization
recollection.intervention: Alloying with 5 at.% rhenium followed by the same heat-treatment schedule
recollection.structure: Single-phase body-centered-cubic solid solution with weak Re enrichment at grain boundaries
recollection.mechanism: Re atoms act as vacancy traps and reduce vacancy mobility, pinning dislocation loops and suppressing void nucleation during irradiation
recollection.results: Under 3 MeV Ni2+ ion irradiation to 10 dpa at 500 °C, the Re-doped alloy showed a 45 % reduction in dislocation-loop density (from ~4×10^22 m^–3 to ~2.2×10^22 m^–3), a drop in irradiation-induced swelling from ~0.8 % to ~0.3 %, and a 15 % lower hardness increase compared to the Re-free alloy

score.note: The recollection captures only the title-level idea of adding Re and correctly mentions a single-phase BCC structure. However, it incorrectly gives 5 at.% Re instead of equiatomic NbMoTaWRe, arc-melted bulk material instead of sputtered nanocrystalline films, and Ni irradiation/heat treatment instead of 120 keV He implantation. It misses the Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions. The proposed vacancy-trapping/dislocation-loop mechanism conflicts with the reported defect-sink and vacancy-annihilation mechanism suppressing He-bubble segregation. All numerical irradiation conditions and outcomes are unrelated to the paper.
